svg.text: Budgeted controllability-aware reachability trees as world models
A useful world model should allocate finite prediction compute over controllability-distinct executable futures, rather than predicting a single trajectory or a flat set of successor states.
LayerNorm + SiLU. Only the (obs_dim, z_dim) contract is
relied on downstream, so a CNN for pixels is a drop-in
shared trunk + one linear head per temporal scale, each
L2-normalised so d_q stays bounded in [0, 2] and cannot
q = C(z) is a deterministic function of z, so it cannot
hold more information about the future than z does. Any
q advantage is a claim about metric geometry — which is
why it is tested against a control rather than assumed.
AUXILIARY HEADS · OUTSIDE THE TREE LOOP
All eleven arms share these encoders and train them
identically, which is what makes the coverage metric
comparable across arms. It is still decoded latents,
not a simulator ground-truth reachable set.
one network reused at every depth · branch_transformer.py · latent_dynamics.py
⊕ depth embedding — the only positional signal
3 × pre-norm self-attention · d_model 256 · 4 heads · GELU FFN ×4
Siblings are contextualised: branch 3 can learn “go right” because branches 1 and 2 already took the other modes. Without sibling
attention the K heads collapse onto the dominant mode — exactly the failure FlatKWM exists to avoid.
out: K contextualised branch embeddings b_i ∈ R²⁵⁶
six plain MLP heads — diffusion / DiT action decoders are out of scope until simple heads have been tested
σ(·) — a score, NOT a probability
κ and ρ are separate heads on purpose. Support asks “is this a distinct supported future?”; mass asks “how common is it?”. Conflating
them ranks modes by frequency and silently deletes the rare ones.
z′_i = z + MLP[ z ‖ enc(A_i ⊙ mask_i) ‖ emb(h_i) ‖ b_i ]
The action chunk is a genuine input, masked before flattening so the chunk length cannot be read off the padding pattern. A branch
therefore cannot claim a consequence its own actions do not produce — which is what makes the bind loss mean something.

expands in lockstep, so nothing recurses in the hot loop.

Every tree arm shares one expansion loop and one set of weights. This ranking function is the only
thing that changes between arms, which is what makes “learned allocation” a one-variable comparison.

dropped are the ones the model considers least supported — never a silent tail truncation by slot

THE SEVEN ARMS — ONE NETWORK, ONE AXIS

Every arm is the same network class with the same components and matched capacity (3.67 M parameters; FlatKWM 3.70 M for its extra branch tokens). They differ in three settings only, and the tree arms differ in

heuristictreewm is not in the original spec and was added deliberately. BFS and random are non-adaptive; uncertainty keys off a different signal. None of them separates adaptive from learned, so without this arm a
TreeWM win over FixedTreeWM is equally well explained by “any novelty heuristic beats breadth-first”.
Experiment 2 pushes the same logic further and pairs each learned arm with the direct heuristic computing the identical signal: noveltyq ↔ learnedq, noveltyz ↔ learnedz.
THE TREE, UNDER A HARD BUDGET
treewm/tree/node.py — exactly node_budget chunk-nodes, for every arm
One tree. Built without the goal, then scored with it.
filled nodes = the executed root-to-n* path · ring = selected node
Every arm emits exactly node_budget nodes — only the shape differs
tests/test_tree.py::test_node_budget_enforced_for_every_arm asserts parity for all seven arms at three
budgets, and sweep_budgets re-asserts it at evaluation time. Without it, “TreeWM beats FlatKWM at N = 64”
would only mean “16× more nodes wins”.

Everything above runs under torch.no_grad at inference. Every parameter — E_φ, C_η, BranchTransformer, BranchHeads, F_θ and g_ψ — comes from the objectives below, and every target below is derived from offline data rather than from the model itself.
pointmaze-medium · navigate / stitch · normalised (s, a). On the stitch split (5 000 trajectories ×
200 steps) no single trajectory spans a geodesically distant start/goal pair, so success requires
k-d tree over normalised raw state — stable from step 1, unlike a moving learned latent. 24
neighbours within radius 1.0, excluding the same trajectory within ±50 steps: those share a
continuation and would only inflate the dominant mode.
borrow their continuations, choose a horizon
h ∈ {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}: the first horizon whose displacement exceeds 0.25. A mode's duration is how
long the state takes to actually go somewhere, so the horizon head predicts something other than a
average linkage, distance threshold 0.25 → ≈3 modes per anchor, cap 8. PointMaze is deterministic
with a continuous action space, so the reachable set is a continuum: the partition has to be
Truncation past the cap is random, never mass-ordered — dropping the smallest clusters would delete
exactly the rare-but-valid modes this project exists to preserve. Nothing in this module reads maze

Each mode also yields one executable representative future (A*, h*, endpoint) — a real action chunk,
AND THE TARGET FOR THE GAIN HEAD
novelty (current default): min_j d(q_n, q_j) — the exact signal the winning parameter-free
heuristic acts on, which makes “direct vs learned” one variable.
retrieval (original): | { endpoint cells of z_n's dataset neighbours } \ cells(T) | — how many new
regions of the world become reachable if this node is expanded.
Both are model-independent and exist at step 1. Supervising G against “a more exhaustive teacher
expansion” would bootstrap a self-graded signal off noise: at initialisation the teacher is the
Hungarian matching: K branches ↔ C modes
Optimal one-to-one assignment, greedy kept for ablations. Action distance is masked to each target's horizon so a
branch is not penalised for padding, and unmatched branches are masked out of every per-branch loss. This is the
hinge between the data-side definition of a mode and the model-side notion of a branch.
successor latent against the matched mode endpoint
push the target chunk through F_θ: the successor must depend on the actions, not be read off z alone
expanding a predicted latent must stay consistent
every supported mode must be covered by some branch
future-set distance (default) | contrastive | bootstrap — states are close in q iff their retrieved
g_ψ regressed on G*, plus the context-free prior G_i on the root's children. The tree is grown under
no_grad, so the model cannot lower the loss by degrading its own tree
Auxiliary terms ramp in linearly — mass 1 k, expand 2 k, redundancy 5 k steps. This is not cosmetic: before the branch
heads differentiate, every sibling pair has d_q ≈ 0, so exp(−d_q/τ) ≈ 1 and Σ κ_i κ_j is minimised by driving every κ
to zero. Observed directly as an effective branching factor pinned at 0.00 for a whole run, and fixed by the ramp.
Every term is independently switchable and independently weighted, and a disabled term is skipped rather than
zero-weighted — so an ablation cannot pay for a loss it is not using.
DIAGNOSTICS THAT CAN FALSIFY THE CLAIM
THE CAUSAL CHAIN, ONE LINK AT A TIME
vs node budget ∈ {16, 32, 64, 128, 256} on the hard split — start/goal pairs in the top
geodesic-distance quartile. The primary, compute-normalised metric.
distinct quantised regions reached per node, scored by one global quantiser shared across
arms, so a model cannot look good by redefining the space it is measured in.
q against z, and against a frozen random projection of z at matched dimension. Negative
in all 42 runs: the metric geometry is not there.
does g_ψ actually predict its own target? Spearman 0.80–0.91 under the novelty target, so
the regression is not the weak link.
does the effective branching factor track empirical local future diversity? +0.42
navigate / +0.82 stitch — but identical across arms, so it is a property of the shared
branch network rather than of any allocation policy.
execute every sampled node's root-to-node chunks in the simulator and compare against the
decoded prediction. Region counts are honest (ratio 1.03–1.10); the node → position
Open-loop error compounds with depth and is essentially arm-independent: d1 ≈ 0.1 → d4 ≈
1.3 → d8 ≈ 3.9 world units, against a maze corridor width of 4.0. Novelty-driven
allocation converts budget into depth and depth into error, so coverage and planning
utility are in tension under an imperfect chunk-level model. That is where the evidence
points next: trade novelty against reliability using the uncertainty head that already
one tree of exactly node_budget nodes
Built so the causal chain can be falsified one link at a time: FlatKWM > SingleWM → FixedTree > FlatKWM → q-coverage > z-coverage → TreeWM > FixedTree.
